actors.name: Nightfall Syndicate
actors.motivation: Extortion at scale, with data theft as leverage
actors.description: A mature extortion operation that buys access rather than earning it, favours managed service providers and privileged identities, and negotiates professionally.

actors.name: Grey Harbour
actors.description: High-volume, low-sophistication and relentless. Works through exposed applications, phishing and credential reuse, and sells on what it cannot use.

actors.name: Silent Meridian
actors.motivation: Long-term access to commercially sensitive data
actors.description: Patient and quiet. Interested in the behavioural data lake and the acquisition pipeline. Would rather stay for a year than be noticed in a week.

actors.name: Black Tern
actors.motivation: Visible disruption of payments and logistics, for political effect
actors.description: Works for a cause rather than a payout. Wants an outage people notice, chooses the services that make the news, and has nothing to negotiate.

incidentFamilies.name: Ransomware and service encryption
incidentFamilies.description: An extortion actor reaches administrative control and encrypts what the business runs on.
incidentFamilies.headline: Nexora woke up to encrypted infrastructure and a negotiation window.

whatHelped.text: Backups that could not be reached from the compromised accounts

whatHurt.text: Recovery that had never been timed

incidentFamilies.name: Customer data exposure
incidentFamilies.description: Customer records leave the estate through an internet-facing weakness.
incidentFamilies.headline: Customer records left Nexora through a door nobody had looked at recently.

whatHelped.text: Egress monitoring that flagged the volume
Legal engaged from the first hour

whatHurt.text: Data held longer than the retention policy allowed
Weak control over who could query the data

incidentFamilies.name: Targeted data theft
incidentFamilies.description: A patient actor takes commercially sensitive material over a long period.
incidentFamilies.headline: Someone had been reading Nexora's commercial data for months.

whatHelped.text: Telemetry retained long enough to reconstruct the intrusion

whatHurt.text: Detection tuned for noise rather than patience

incidentFamilies.name: Legacy platform compromise and outage
incidentFamilies.description: An unsupported platform is compromised and taken out of service.
incidentFamilies.headline: The warehouse platform stopped, and nobody could say when it would return.

whatHelped.text: A manual fulfilment fallback that had been documented

whatHurt: An unsupported operating system with no patch path

whatHurt.text: No current inventory of the legacy estate

incidentFamilies.name: Supplier-driven disruption
incidentFamilies.description: A supplier's own compromise propagates into Nexora's operations.
incidentFamilies.headline: Nexora's problem started inside somebody else's network.

whatHelped.text: The ability to cut supplier access without cutting the business

whatHurt.text: Integration accounts with more rights than the integration needed

incidentFamilies.name: Destructive attack
incidentFamilies.description: An actor with no interest in money destroys what the business runs on, so that it is seen to stop.
incidentFamilies.headline: Nexora's warehouse systems were wiped, and nobody asked for anything.

whatHelped.text: Backups held where the wiping accounts could not reach
A manual fulfilment fallback that had been documented

whatHurt.text: Administrative reach into the warehouse estate from the corporate network

whatHurt: Nothing to negotiate with, and so no time bought

incidentFamilies.name: Payment diversion
incidentFamilies.description: A compromised account sends Nexora's money somewhere it should not go.
incidentFamilies.headline: Nexora paid somebody else, on instructions that looked like its own.

whatHelped.text: A second factor on the accounts that move money

whatHurt.text: Bank detail changes accepted on the strength of an email

incidentFamilies.name: Customer platform tampering
incidentFamilies.description: An actor changes what customers see or send, through the platform's own release process.
incidentFamilies.headline: Customers used a Nexora checkout that Nexora had not written.

whatHelped.text: A cloud estate whose configuration was checked rather than trusted

whatHurt.text: A pipeline that deployed whatever reached it

attackPaths.name: Managed service provider to production
attackPaths.summary: Compromise of provider credentials, in through vendor remote access, up through privileged identity, out across production.

steps.narrative: A provider engineer's credentials are obtained and reused.
Vendor remote access accepts the session without challenge.
A standing administrative account in the identity platform is used to mint further access.
Jump servers give a route into production administration.
Production workloads and their backups are encrypted together.

attackPaths.name: Phishing into the legacy estate
attackPaths.summary: A phished endpoint, a flat corporate network, and an unsupported warehouse platform.

steps.narrative: A finance user opens an invoice attachment.
The device is used to reach broader corporate infrastructure.
An unsupported system in the legacy data centre is trivially exploited.
The warehouse platform is encrypted mid-shift.

attackPaths.name: Internet-facing application to customer data
attackPaths.summary: An exposed weakness in checkout, then a straight line to the customer record store.

steps.narrative: A weakness in the checkout service is found and exploited.
Container workload identity is over-permissioned.
Customer records are queried in bulk and extracted.

attackPaths.name: Partner portal credential abuse
attackPaths.summary: Reused partner credentials, a portal that shares an identity platform with staff.

steps.narrative: Reused partner credentials succeed against the extranet.
The partner identity turns out to sit in the same directory as staff.
Order and customer data is pulled through the integration.

attackPaths.name: Engineering pipeline to production
attackPaths.summary: A developer workstation, the build pipeline, and standing deployment credentials.

steps.narrative: An engineer is targeted with a convincing package-related lure.
Pipeline credentials are harvested and a build step is modified.
The pipeline deploys the actor's access straight into production.

attackPaths.name: Quiet route to the data lake
attackPaths.summary: A phished analyst, federated access, and a data lake nobody monitors.

steps.narrative: An analyst's session is stolen rather than their password.
Broad standing read access across the platform is inherited.
Behavioural data is extracted slowly enough not to trip anything.

attackPaths.name: Logistics partner into order management
attackPaths.summary: A supplier's compromise arrives through an integration nobody documented.

steps.narrative: The logistics partner is compromised in its own estate.
The integration account turns out to have far more than read access.
Fulfilment data is corrupted and despatch stops.

attackPaths.name: Non-production into production
attackPaths.summary: Loose non-production controls and a peering link that should not exist.

steps.narrative: A test environment exposed to the internet is taken over.
The peering link carries the actor into the production tenancy.
Customer records are copied out through cloud storage.

attackPaths.name: Through the remote access appliance to the warehouses
attackPaths.summary: An unpatched appliance at the edge, an identity platform that trusts it, and administrative reach into the warehouse estate.

steps.narrative: A published flaw in the remote access appliance gives a foothold at the edge.
Sessions taken from the appliance are traded for administrative identities.
The jump servers give reach into the warehouse estate.
The warehouse systems are wiped, with no note left behind.

attackPaths.name: Through the build pipeline to the checkout
attackPaths.summary: An engineer's laptop, a pipeline that deploys whatever it is given, and a checkout customers trust.

steps.narrative: An engineer installs a package that does more than it says.
A change is slipped into the pipeline's own configuration.
The next release ships the actor's code to every customer.

attackPaths.name: Through a finance mailbox to a supplier payment
attackPaths.summary: A phished finance user, a mailbox rule nobody set, and bank details changed on an email.

steps.narrative: A finance user signs in to a page that only looks like Nexora's.
The stolen session sets a quiet forwarding rule on the mailbox.
A supplier's bank details are changed, on the strength of an email from the supplier.

attackPaths.name: Through the HR provider to payroll
attackPaths.summary: A breached HR supplier, staff passwords reused at work, and payroll details nobody checks twice.

steps.narrative: Staff credentials taken from the HR provider's breach are tried at Nexora.
Reused passwords open accounts that never enrolled a second factor.
Salary payments are redirected to accounts the staff do not own.

attackPaths.name: Through a forgotten service account to the backups
attackPaths.summary: A service account nobody owns, a backup platform administered with the same rights, and production with nothing left to restore from.

steps.narrative: An old service account's password, unchanged in years, still works.
The same rights administer the backups, which are deleted first.
Production is encrypted with nothing behind it to restore from.

attackPaths.name: Through Kestrel to the deal room
attackPaths.summary: An acquisition that arrived already compromised, a flat corporate network, and the finance system where deals are modelled.

steps.narrative: Access planted at Kestrel before the deal survives the integration.
The corporate network does not tell Kestrel's machines from Nexora's.
Deal models and forecasts leave a little at a time.
